Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the standard hatchling.build PEP 517 backend; no custom build hook or setup.py execution logic was identified.
  • No .pth, sitecustomize.py, or usercustomize.py files were identified.
  • [project.scripts] wraith-mcp = "wraith_mcp.server:main" and wraith_mcp/__main__.py are normal user-invoked entry points. They do not indicate install-time or interpreter-start automatic execution.
  • Import-time behavior in server.py appears limited to MCP object creation and environment-derived configuration values. No malicious side effects such as credential harvesting, exfiltration, or persistence installation were identified.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • Environment variables such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and GOOGLE_API_KEY are documented LLM provider configuration values used for normal SDK initialization. There is no evidence of broad environment harvesting, .env/SSH/cloud/CI token discovery, or file collection.
  • https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 and LLM SDK usage appear to be expected application functionality, not attacker-controlled C2, webhook, or drop-service exfiltration.
  • base64 is used by the screenshot() tool to return PNG screenshot data. No evidence of an obfuscated loader or payload decoding was identified.
  • No archive/staging, temporary credential collection, or external upload logic was identified.
  • No persistence mechanisms such as cron, systemd, LaunchAgents, or shell profile modification were identified.
  • No Kubernetes service-account access, Docker socket use, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection behavior was identified.
  • subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "patchright", "install", "chromium"]) appears to install Patchright Chromium for browser automation. There is no evidence that it runs during package installation; it may be invoked when the user uses browser-related MCP tools, which is consistent with the package’s stated functionality.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • .env.example, .github/workflows/*.yml, and .gitignore are included in the sdist, but their contents do not show malicious workflow logic, CI secret theft, or hidden payload behavior.
  • No unexplained native binaries, obfuscated payloads, or wheel/sdist mismatch evidence was visible in the provided corpus.
  • No direct evidence of dependency confusion, typosquatting, or sudden malicious dependency insertion was identified.

Additional Verification Needed

  • This review is limited to the provided extracted sdist text. If a wheel was also distributed, comparing the wheel against the sdist is recommended.
